dmp.description: The genetic characterization and surveillance of viral evolution is an urgent need at a global level in the context of continuous emergence of viral threats, as recently observed in SARS-CoV-2 and mpox epidemics. The existence of turnkey bioinformatics solutions covering all aspects of sequence data analysis is still an unmet necessity. INSaFLU provides a user-friendly web-based solution enabling researchers with little training in bioinformatics to perform multi-step computational analyses, starting from raw sequencing data. We have been expanding the routine-oriented INSaFLU to include a  metagenomics viral pathogen detection module when the viral threat is unknown. INSaFLU will also be expanded with novel reporting tools facilitating data interpretation and, ultimately, public health decision-making. This project aims at supporting the continuous upgrade of the existing “surveillance-oriented” component and the novel metagenomics virus identification module, as well as ongoing and upcoming national and international training activities of INSaFLU. This support of the development and training activities is expected to be essential to strengthen the functional and  computational performance of the INSaFLU platform, ensuring that it can offer efficient services (for virus detection and monitoring) to the scientific community at national and global scale, contributing to an enhanced capacity building and preparedness for the prevention and control of viral infectious diseases.
